verdict: Holding steady: revenue is down 2% over 30 days (down 31% in the last week) and new customers are up 3%. Repeat buyers carry 35% of the business. The fixes below are mostly cheap and quick.
working: Visitors who arrive still buy: 3.5% of visits turn into orders, down 16% on the previous 30 days.
Ads got cheaper per customer: cost per new customer fell from ₹434 to ₹588 while spend was cut 4%.
Loyal base and a hero product: 39% of buyers are repeat customers, and First Flush Darjeeling Tea alone made ₹2.19L (50% of revenue).
notWorking: Fewer new people are finding us: visits are up 21% and new customers up 3% in 30 days. Last week revenue was down 47%.
Leaks at the till: best-selling 250g packs sold out (12 items out of stock), and ₹2.21L left in unfinished checkouts with only 8% recovered.
Ads also reach people who already buy from us: 4 of 6 campaigns (₹1.22L of spend) don't leave out existing customers.
amazonPublic: Public check (earlier audit): First Flush 250g listing rated 3.6★ from 244 ratings, listed at ₹379 with text that says 100g; the website sells 250g at ₹806.

findings.title: Only 8.1% of unfinished checkouts come back and pay
findings.detail: 255 unfinished checkouts in the last 30 days worth ₹210,597; 20 recovered (₹9,903). ₹98,271 was left unpaid. Over 90 days the rate was 6.9% (81 junk ₹0 checkouts left out).

findings.title: WhatsApp reminders do fire, but 38% of them fail
findings.detail: Checked 37 recent unfinished checkouts in Zoko: all 34 got the same 'payment pending' template, at about 27 minutes and again at about 25 hours. Of 75 sends, 56% failed (18 with WhatsApp error 167918, Meta's limit on marketing messages per person) and 22% were read.

findings.title: Email reminders: one email, about 10 hours later (inferred)
findings.detail: 89% of checkouts with an email were updated almost exactly 10 hours after they started, which matches Shopify's abandoned-checkout email timing. There is no sign of a second or third email. 22% of abandoners gave only a phone number, so email can't reach them.

findings.title: New customers recover at 5.6%, returning at 10%
findings.detail: 153 of 202 abandoners were first-time buyers. They need trust (reviews, delivery time, COD, freshness) more than a reminder.

findings.title: Carts under ₹465 pay ₹43 shipping and almost never come back (4%)
findings.detail: 16 checkouts (13%) were under ₹251; 119% of them were charged ₹63 shipping. Carts of ₹326 and up recovered at 8.7%. The checkout's free-shipping line is effectively ₹313, but the site also says ₹305 in places, and 20% of carts of ₹433 and up still show a ₹58 charge (check whether that is a COD fee).

findings.title: Since Razorpay Magic Checkout went live (week of 21 Sep), Shopify sees fewer abandoned checkouts
findings.detail: Before: 100 a week at 5.8% recovery. After: 35 a week at 8.2%. Checkout-to-order went from 53% to 43%. Shoppers who leave the Razorpay pop-up before typing a phone number never reach Shopify, so the full drop-off is only visible in Razorpay's dashboard.

findings.title: Evening abandoners are the hardest to win back
findings.detail: 80 checkouts (27%) were left between 6 pm and midnight and recovered at 7.2%, against 9.8% for the morning.

findings.title: Stock and price errors are not what's stopping checkouts now
findings.detail: Only 5 of 195 unfinished checkouts in the last 30 days held an item that is sold out today (8% over 90 days). Sold-out 250g packs lose sales earlier, on the product page. No checkout carried a Shopify discount code (Razorpay coupons may not be passed back to Shopify).

gaps: Opt-in / consent status is not exposed by the Zoko API.

findings: Dorje is the value pick for single-estate Darjeeling: First Flush ₹499/100 g vs a ₹1,949 median for the 9 D2C peers checked (Teabox ₹1,502, Vahdam ₹1,885, Tea Culture ₹2,404). Second Flush ₹444–399/100 g is also below most peers. Only Udyan (₹651) and Karma Kettle (₹813) come close on First Flush. Watch: Happy Valley Organic now runs 15 active Meta ads (8 started in the last week; 15 a week ago) with prices in the headline (First Flush ₹982, Second Flush ₹522).

The same Dorje items are 31–36% cheaper on Dorje's own Amazon listings than on dorjeteas.com (e.g. Kahwa 100 g ₹323 on Amazon vs ₹604 on site). Shoppers who compare have a reason to leave the site cart: a likely (not measured) drag on the 8.7% checkout recovery.

Pyramid teabags cost more per bag than most rivals: Dorje ₹21–24/bag on site vs a ₹20 median (Teabox ₹11, Organic India ₹10, Mittal ₹11; only Sancha ₹24 and Tea Culture ₹24 come close). The printed catalogue (₹450/₹499) is the struck-through price; the site sells at ₹360/₹506.
Dorje has the strongest on-site review proof checked (4.63★ from 645 reviews on First Flush) and a rare 7-day taste-replacement promise; most peers refuse taste returns. Neither is used in ads today.

Offers: Teabox and Udyan match Dorje's ₹502 free-shipping line; Teabox, Udyan, Mittal and Organic India push COD. Sancha, Udyan and Vahdam add free samples with orders; Tea Culture shows a 'free shipping in ₹X' cart bar. Dorje has none of the sample offers.

Meta: Vahdam runs ~461 active India ads (offer-led, mostly supplements); Dorje ~39 (story-led); Teabox 27 (scarcity 'last 449 units'). Udyan has no active Meta ads; Karma Kettle was not re-checked this week.

Search: Dorje is in Google's top 3 for 6 of 9 key searches (#1 'second flush darjeeling tea', #2 'first flush… buy online' and 'muscatel'), but is not in the top 12 for 'organic darjeeling tea' or 'single estate darjeeling tea', the two phrases that describe Dorje best. Google's AI answers name Dorje in 2 of 8; for 'best darjeeling tea' they cite Sancha and Goodricke. On Amazon, Makaibari, Gopaldhara and Goodricke own 'darjeeling tea' and 'darjeeling first flush tea'; Dorje is now sponsored #2/#4 (and #7 not sponsored) for 'darjeeling first flush tea' and #5 sponsored for 'darjeeling tea' (not in the top 13 last week).

patterns: The offer goes in the headline. Vahdam ("Up to 34% off + free gifts"), Mittal ("@₹465"), Happy Valley ("Second Flush, ₹226") and Jay Shree ("8% off for first-time buyers") all put a price or % in the headline. Dorje shows an offer in 1 of its sampled ads, and only in the sub-line.

Free gifts and samples are everywhere: Vahdam gives free minis and a full-size gift as the order grows, Sancha 2 samples + coasters, Udyan 3 samples, Organic India a ₹186 mystery gift, Teabox 3 freebies with its gift pack. Dorje has none.
A 9–6% first-order code is standard (Golden Tips 9%, Sancha 11%, Kaahu 9%, Jay Shree 7%), shown in the banner or an email form. Dorje shows no first-order offer or email/WhatsApp popup.

The biggest spenders sell benefits, not origin: Vahdam, Organic India, Tea Culture and Sancha lead with sleep, throat, joints, skin and weight. Only Kaahu, Golden Tips, Happy Valley and Jay Shree lead with the garden.
Retargeting uses catalogue ads with the price and a "restock" nudge (Goodricke). Tea Culture and Organic India also send ad traffic to Blinkit, Zepto and Amazon.

Seasonal bursts: Teabox started all 21 Diwali ads on one day; Happy Valley has a Pujo hook; Golden Tips and Sancha are already on Christmas. Dorje's banner has dropped "Diwali" but is still the old 23% over ₹654 offer; Organic India moved from a Diwali to a Winter Wellness sale.
Long-running ads (likely winners): Sancha's mint masala chai video (~352 days), Goodricke's catalogue ads (~172 days), Golden Tips' range carousel (~93 days).

ao.test: Test plan (estimate): run 3 creatives per angle for 14 days with buyer exclusions on. Judge on cost per purchase and ROAS against the ~1.6 baseline. Pause an angle when it has spent about 3× the target cost per purchase without beating the baseline, and move its budget to the winner. Suggested split of Meta budget: 53% prospecting (moves 1–2, Advantage+ broad), 22% retargeting/catalogue (move 5), 11% wellness teabags (move 6), 11% seasonal gifting (move 7).
ao.method: Meta: Meta Ad Library, country India, active ads; counts are Meta's estimate. "Running since" is only shown when every active ad was returned. Google: Ads Transparency Center, region India, last 30 days, by website. Offers: each homepage with India store settings on 14 Nov 2026 (banner, popup, cart). Amazon: amazon.in search cards. Strategy lines and the playbook are our analysis; budget splits and impacts are estimates.

atr.apiMethod: Estimated ad pressure index (0–106, relative to the busiest brand): 33% active Meta ads in India (log), 13% launch cadence (new ads per week, log), 12% median age of sampled ads, 11% variants per concept × multi-version share, 12% placement breadth. It is an ESTIMATE of visible ad activity, not reach, impressions or spend — Meta does not publish those for commercial ads in India.
limits: Meta publishes reach only for ads shown in the EU/UK and spend/impressions only for political or social-issue ads; India commercial ads have neither. Google Ads Transparency shows ad counts, formats and regions but no impressions for commercial ads.

Format/placement/CTA mix comes from the first ~17–37 ad cards Meta shows logged out (identical ads are grouped, so "covered" counts the ads those cards represent). Vahdam and Organic India have hundreds of ads, so theirs is the newest slice only. Makaibari's Ad Library page did not load logged out.
Catalogue/DPA and Collection ads cannot be told apart reliably from the public card; "shows prices" flags cards with two or more ₹ prices. "Multiple versions" means dynamic/flexible creative.
Instagram post engagement (likes/comments per post) is not readable without logging in, so only follower and post counts are shown.
Similarweb numbers are third-party modelled estimates for October 2026, not measured traffic.
takeaways: On visible Meta activity Dorje is already third of 13 (estimated pressure index 62), behind only Vahdam (91) and Organic India (74) and ahead of every Darjeeling estate brand. More ads won't fix much; making the current spend work harder will.

Instagram Reels took ₹34,773 at ROAS 0.75, the weakest big placement. Facebook Feed (1.85), Facebook Reels (1.73) and Stories do better. Move Reels budget to Feed and Stories, or rebuild the Reels creative.

WhatsApp marketing messages took ₹41,385 (about a quarter of Meta spend) at about ₹1.6 per impression and ROAS 1.42. Sancha and Mittal use click-to-WhatsApp ads into their own chat instead. Test click-to-WhatsApp into Zoko against the paid message placement.

By format, Dorje's single-image ads (ROAS 2.06) and flexible ads (1.86) beat video/Reels (1.24), which get the most spend. Most peers lean on single images (Sancha 55%, Organic India 59%, Tea Culture 75%). Shift spend toward price-and-proof statics.

Low-quality placements are being hit over and over: Audience Network frequency 9.2, right column 12, WhatsApp Status 9. Exclude them or cap frequency. Golden Tips and Sancha keep evergreen ads running 2–3 months (median age 108 and 56 days); Dorje's evergreen winners should get the same treatment instead of being relaunched in batches.
